A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of label smoothing, selective classification and logit normalisation. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on ImageNet, ImageNet-Sketch, Cityscapes and CIFAR-100, including selective-classification performance and logit analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports revised original vision experiments and additional tabular and text classification results on Bank Marketing, Online Shoppers and IMDB.

M1.justification: v2 explicitly omits logit centering from its normalisation procedure. v3 incorporates per-sample mean subtraction through s = -mean(v) in Eq. (16) and Appendix C.5. The remaining label-smoothing and normalised-logit procedures are retained.

E1.justification: Appendices B.4–B.5 add evaluated tabular binary classification on Bank Marketing and Online Shoppers, and sentiment classification on IMDB. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained vision tasks. CIFAR-10 is mentioned as a reproducibility demo, without a new reported benchmark result.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including CE versus LS and comparisons involving MSP, DOCTOR, entropy and Energy. The new tabular/text experiments reuse CE versus LS. TabTransformer supplies a setting reference; negative label smoothing has no completed comparative results.

E3.justification: ImageNet changes from a 50,000-image training holdout for validation and the original validation set for evaluation to a 10,000/40,000 split of that original validation set. CIFAR-100 similarly switches from a training holdout to a 2,000/8,000 test-set split. DeepLab training changes from batch size 12 for 40,000 steps to 16 for 30,000 steps. New binary experiments introduce alpha = 0.6 and additional training protocols; Appendix C explicitly reports retraining.

E4.justification: Appendix F.3 adds a limited empirical diagnostic supporting the centering choice: the per-sample logit mean averages approximately 0.003 with standard deviation 0.001. Existing LS-strength, distribution-shift, conditional-logit and segmentation-error analyses are retained, with revised outputs.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly states that models were retrained with different random seeds. It supplies neither seed values nor repeated-run counts, and adds no across-run confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing sliding-window mean and standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Results are replaced across the retained vision experiments following retraining and setting changes. For example, Cityscapes AURCs at alpha = 0.2/0.3 change from 0.96/1.05 to 0.93/0.90 in Fig. 3, reversing that pair's ordering. New Figs. 17–18 add tabular/text results, including IMDB AURC 3.82 for CE versus 4.50 for LS. The replaced scores do not establish same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Appendix F.5 adds a focused theoretical extension to negative smoothing, with Eqs. (29)–(30) arguing that one-hot labels yield unattainable smoothed targets and an objective unbounded below. The original LS gradient analysis and positive-logit normalisation inequality and proof remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: LS harms selective classification through imbalanced max-logit suppression, and post-hoc logit normalisation can counteract this effect. Added experiments support these retained claims; replacing 'regularisation' with 'suppression' does not redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 adds localized qualifications about weaker tabular effects and unreliable risk-curve estimation with few errors, a fuller rationale for centering potentially negative logits, and possible instability of negative LS. Appendix H expands practical implications and future directions. The limitations illustrated by segmentation failures were already present in v2.

D1.justification: v2 promises future code and model releases; v3 reports their release and supplies explicit GitHub and Hugging Face access links, a CIFAR-10 demo and plotting notebooks. Appendix C adds TorchUncertainty and binary-loss implementation information, tabular/text architectures and preprocessing, double-precision logit calculations, and updated hardware specifications. Resource availability is assessed as reported in the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds substantive engagement with Wei et al. (2022) on negative label smoothing, plus references supporting the tabular/text experiments and implementation, including TabTransformer, LSTM, GloVe and TorchUncertainty. The main positioning relative to prior selective-classification and logit-normalisation research is retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v3 standardizes 'suppression gradient' terminology, clarifies explanations, adds a notation glossary and acknowledgments, and locally reorganizes and expands the appendices.

P2.justification: v3 adds glossary Table 1 and result Figures 17–18; the previous Table 1 becomes Table 2, and previous Figures 17–23 become Figures 19–25. Retained plots and segmentation panels have revised axes, legends, captions and normalisation labels, with some relocation. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new non-vision experiments provide useful additional support for generality, while explicit code/model access information and fuller implementation details improve reproducibility. Added qualifications also clarify practical limits. These gains remain incremental: the central argument is retained, and the new tabular evidence uses strong smoothing and reduced training data while acknowledging substantial variability without quantifying it across repeated runs.
